I finished Standard 7, so I can read the labels on the fertilizer bags, but I still do what my father taught me unless I see it work on my neighbor's plot first. I will spread two ox-cart loads of cattle manure on this 1.52-hectare plot because manure costs nothing and helps the soil hold water when the rains stop early. I will also buy one bag of DAP and one bag of urea from the agro-dealer — that works out to about 21 kg of nitrogen per hectare — because last season my cousin's sorghum heads were much bigger where he put fertilizer. I will use improved sorghum seed that he gave me, but I will not spray chemicals or irrigate; my family will weed by hand for about 130 days this season, and I will hire labor for 15 days at planting and harvest when the work is too much for us.
